grh_c9f93105e081a01c6b8c.title: The Human Comedy
paragraphs: Teenager Homer Macauley works as a bicycle messenger in wartime Ithaca, carrying the small joys and devastating news of his neighbors while his older brother Marcus serves overseas. Through school, family and the telegraph office, Homer learns that becoming a man means recognizing both difference and shared humanity. Elderly telegrapher Willie Grogan dies at his desk just as the message arrives that Marcus has been killed in the war. Before Homer can bring the telegram home, Marcus's wounded Army friend Tobey arrives in Ithaca, saying Marcus made him part of the family. Homer tears up the death notice and welcomes Tobey into the Macauley home as the living piece of his brother that has returned.

This [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]] broadcast aired on September 9, 1949. It is listed as episode 33 in the archive. [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Barton Yarborough, Mickey Rooney, Richard Allen Simmons, Francis X. Bushman, and Howard Esterbrook.
The surviving recording runs about 29 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.7c3febcb3d847984|Pabst Blue Ribbon Beer]].
This version presents a radio version of [[work|work.sdp.film.625866f615b4bc8a|The Human Comedy]]. William Saroyan is credited as author.

grh_c99b750149f8c1cd4316.title: Words at War 43-06-24 (01) Combined Operations
paragraphs: An imaginative reconstruction based on Combined Operations follows a British soldier who volunteers for commando service, survives punishing training and joins a raid on the German-held French coast. The raiders demolish military installations while suffering heavy losses, and a delayed explosive charge aboard the HMS Campbeltown later destroys the dock area and kills German personnel examining the ship. The narrator frames the raid as preparation for the larger assault on Hitler's occupied Europe and as a tribute to the men who died gaining that experience.

paragraphs: A family rents an elegant country house for an implausibly low price, despite the strange behavior of its elderly caretaker and their young son’s uneasiness. The boy begins witnessing spectral scenes of a mother and daughter being murdered twenty years earlier, and the visions expose the caretaker as the killer who now intends to silence the new witnesses.
